To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the absolute Helmholtz energy of the LJ crystal can be accurately predicted by using a combination of the harmonic approximation and a perturbative approach based on the cluster expansion, and (ii) the free energy can be obtained by using a simple and accurate analytical form of the pair correlation function, which is obtained from the solution of the Ornstein-Zernike equation for the direct correlation function.

(i) the free energy of the solid can be calculated accurately by using the anharmonic free energy functional and the pair correlation function, (ii) this free energy functional can be used to predict the sublimation and the melting lines of the solid, (iii) the anharmonic corrections to the free energy are very important for the quantitative description of phase equilibria of the LJ crystal.
the absolute Helmholtz (internal) energy of highly anarmonic crystals can be calculated with high precision and that this energy is in excellent agreement with the results of computer simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the problem of the accurate theoretical prediction of the free energy of classical solids.
the development of a new theory for the calculation of the free energy of classical solids.
the problem of the theoretical prediction of the free energy for highly anharmonic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theoretical prediction of the Helmholtz energy for highly anharmonic classical systems is now possible to an accuracy that is comparable to computer simulation.

, in the absence of the first-principles calculation of the free energy of solids, the theory of the free energy based on the anharmonic lattice dynamics is a very good tool for the prediction of the absolute Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies of solids in the whole temperature range of interest.
the present theoretical method provides a quantitative description of the absolute Helmholtz energy of highly anarmonic crystals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the free energy of the LJ crystal is calculated accurately and in the whole range from zero up to the melting line while accounting for both anharmonic vibrations and the pair correlations in atomic displacements.
the absolute Helmholtz energy of a classical solid can be accurately predicted from the knowledge of interatomic potentials and the lattice structure.
we developed a theory that is able to predict the Helmholtz energy of the LJ solid with accuracy of better than 0.5% over the entire range of temperatures and pressures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anharmonic corrections to free energy are very important and cannot be ignored even at low temperatures and densities.
the free energy of the LJ crystal is well described by the anharmonic free energy functional which is constructed from the phonon frequencies calculated at the harmonic level.
the absolute Helmholtz energy of a crystal can be accurately predicted by using the free energy functional of the harmonic crystal and a simple correction for anharmonicity.
